title: A Two-Stage Pretraining-Finetuning Framework for Treatment Effect Estimation with Unmeasured Confounding

problem.claim: Estimate the conditional average treatment effect from observational data when unmeasured confounding may be present.

gap.claim: Existing studies mainly rely on strong ignorability, while observational data cannot test for unmeasured confounders and RCT data are usually small.

contributions.claim: A two-stage pretraining-finetuning framework combines large-scale observational data with small-scale RCT data for CATE estimation under unmeasured confounding.
The framework trains a foundational covariate representation on observational data and an augmented representation on RCT data to adjust for unmeasured confounding.
A partial parameter initialization approach is used to reduce overfitting from small-scale RCT data instead of training a separate network.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the approach was validated on two public datasets with extensive experiments.
The authors report that code is available.

narrative_sequence.summary: CATE estimation from observational data is important across several application areas.
Unmeasured confounding undermines methods relying on strong ignorability, while RCTs avoid confounding but are typically small.
The proposed framework pretrains a covariate representation with large-scale observational data and fine-tunes an augmented representation with RCT data.
Partial parameter initialization is introduced to limit overfitting in the RCT stage.
The authors report validation on two public datasets and provide code.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines large observational data for representation learning with smaller randomized data for confounding adjustment.

interpretation.claim: Separating broad representation learning from randomized-data adjustment may help address limited randomized sample sizes.

application.claim: Consider staged learning when large observational datasets and smaller randomized datasets are jointly available.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when the staged approach fails or how performance depends on the severity of unmeasured confounding.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, experimental results, or quantitative improvements.
The abstract does not describe theoretical guarantees or the conditions under which unmeasured confounding is successfully adjusted.
